The sum of the first and third term of an arithmetic progression is 12 and the product of the first and second term is 24, then the first term is
solution: \(a+(a+2d)=12\Rightarrow a+d=6\). Product \(a(a+d)=24\Rightarrow 6a=24\Rightarrow a=4\). Matches option C.

stem: If the pth term of an AP is q and its qth term is p, then its \((p+q)\)th term is
solution: \(a+(p-1)d=q\) and \(a+(q-1)d=p\) give \(d=-1\) and \(a=p+q-1\). \(T_{p+q}=a+(p+q-1)d=(p+q-1)-(p+q-1)=0\). Matches option D.

stem: The 15th term from the end in \(4, 7, 10, 13, \ldots, 154\) is
solution: With last term 154 and \(d=3\), the nth term from the end is \(l-(n-1)d=154-14\times 3=154-42=112\). Matches option B.

stem: In an A.P., the first term is 1, the last term is 11 and the sum of n terms is 36, then \(n=\)
solution: \(S=\dfrac{n}{2}(a+l)=\dfrac{n}{2}(1+11)=6n=36\Rightarrow n=6\). Matches option B.

stem: If the sum of n terms of an A.P. is \(3n^2+5n\) and \(T_m=164\), then m equals
solution: \(T_n=S_n-S_{n-1}=(3n^2+5n)-\left(3(n-1)^2+5(n-1)\right)=6n+2\). Setting \(6m+2=164\) gives \(m=27\). Matches option B.

stem: If the mth term of an A.P. is \(\dfrac{1}{n}\) and the nth term is \(\dfrac{1}{m}\), then find the sum of mn terms.
solution: From \(a+(m-1)d=\dfrac1n\) and \(a+(n-1)d=\dfrac1m\) we get \(a=d=\dfrac{1}{mn}\). Then \(S_{mn}=\dfrac{mn}{2}\left[2a+(mn-1)d\right]=\dfrac{mn}{2}\cdot\dfrac{mn+1}{mn}=\dfrac{mn+1}{2}\). Matches option A.

stem: If the nth term of an AP is \(\dfrac{1}{3}(2n+1)\), then the sum of its first 19 terms is
solution: \(T_1=1\), \(d=\dfrac23\). \(S_{19}=\dfrac{19}{2}\left[2(1)+18\cdot\dfrac23\right]=\dfrac{19}{2}(14)=133\). Matches option C.

stem: The sum of all integers between 81 and 719 which are divisible by 5 is
solution: The multiples run \(85, 90, \ldots, 715\); count \(=\dfrac{715-85}{5}+1=127\). Sum \(=\dfrac{127}{2}(85+715)=127\times 400=50800\). Matches option B.

stem: Three numbers are in A.P. whose sum is 33 and product is 792, then the smallest number from these numbers is
solution: Take \(a-d, a, a+d\): sum \(3a=33\Rightarrow a=11\). Product \(11(121-d^2)=792\Rightarrow d^2=49\Rightarrow d=7\). Numbers \(4, 11, 18\); smallest is 4. Matches option A.

stem: If \(a, b, c, d, e\) are in A.P., then the value of \(a-4b+6c-4d+e\) is
solution: With equal spacing the coefficients \(1,-4,6,-4,1\) sum to zero for both the constant and the common-difference parts, so \(a-4b+6c-4d+e=0\). Matches option C.

stem: If \(a, b, c\) are in AP, then \((a-c)^2\) equals
solution: In AP, \(a+c=2b\). \((a-c)^2=(a+c)^2-4ac=(2b)^2-4ac=4(b^2-ac)\). Matches option A.

stem: If angles of a quadrilateral are in A.P. with common difference \(10^\circ\), then the smallest angle is
solution: The four angles \(a, a+10, a+20, a+30\) sum to \(360^\circ\): \(4a+60=360\Rightarrow a=75^\circ\). Matches option B.

subtopic: Harmonic Progressions and the Three Means
stem: If the sum of the resulting series obtained by introducing n A.M.'s between 2 and 38 is 200, then n is equal to
solution: The full series has \(n+2\) terms with sum \(\dfrac{n+2}{2}(2+38)=20(n+2)=200\Rightarrow n+2=10\Rightarrow n=8\). Matches option C.

subtopic: Harmonic Progressions and the Three Means
stem: n AM's are inserted between 7 and 71. If the fifth AM is 27, then n is equal to
solution: The AMs form an AP with common difference \(d=\dfrac{71-7}{n+1}\). Fifth AM \(=7+5d=27\Rightarrow d=4\), so \(\dfrac{64}{n+1}=4\Rightarrow n=15\). Matches option C.

subtopic: Harmonic Progressions and the Three Means
stem: If 8 arithmetic means are placed between 2 and 17, then the 5th arithmetic mean will be
solution: \(d=\dfrac{17-2}{8+1}=\dfrac{5}{3}\). 5th AM \(=2+5\cdot\dfrac{5}{3}=2+\dfrac{25}{3}=\dfrac{31}{3}\). Matches option C.

subtopic: Harmonic Progressions and the Three Means
stem: Sum of 20 arithmetic means between 1 and 99 is
solution: Sum of n AMs between a and b is \(\dfrac{n(a+b)}{2}=\dfrac{20(1+99)}{2}=1000\). Matches option B.

stem: If \(x\), \(2x+2\) and \(3x+3\) are in GP, then its 4th term is
solution: \((2x+2)^2=x(3x+3)\Rightarrow x^2+5x+4=0\Rightarrow x=-1\) or \(x=-4\). \(x=-1\) is degenerate; \(x=-4\) gives \(-4, -6, -9\) with \(r=\dfrac32\), so the 4th term \(=-9\times\dfrac32=-13.5\). Matches option D.

stem: The sixth term of a G.P. is 32 and its 8th term is 128, then its common ratio is
solution: \(\dfrac{T_8}{T_6}=r^2=\dfrac{128}{32}=4\Rightarrow r=\pm 2\). Matches option B.

stem: If \(y=1+x+x^2+\ldots\) up to infinite terms, then x is equal to
solution: \(y=\dfrac{1}{1-x}\) for \(|x|<1\), so \(1-x=\dfrac1y\) and \(x=\dfrac{y-1}{y}\). Matches option A.

stem: If the nth term of \(5, \sqrt5, 1, \ldots\) is \(\dfrac{1}{625}\), then the value of n is
solution: First term \(5\), ratio \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt5}\). \(T_n=5\cdot 5^{-(n-1)/2}=5^{1-(n-1)/2}=5^{-4}\Rightarrow 1-\dfrac{n-1}{2}=-4\Rightarrow n=11\). Matches option C.

stem: If the first term of a G.P. is 1 and the sum of its 3rd and 5th term is 90, then the common ratio is
solution: \(r^2+r^4=90\). Let \(u=r^2\): \(u^2+u-90=0\Rightarrow u=9\Rightarrow r=\pm 3\). Matches option B.

stem: Sum of 9 terms of the G.P. \(1-\dfrac12+\dfrac14-\dfrac18+\ldots\) is
solution: First term 1, ratio \(-\dfrac12\). \(S_9=\dfrac{1-\left(-\tfrac12\right)^9}{1+\tfrac12}=\dfrac{1+\tfrac{1}{512}}{\tfrac32}=\dfrac{513/512}{3/2}=\dfrac{171}{256}\). Matches option A.

stem: The value of \(5^{1/2}\cdot 5^{1/4}\cdot 5^{1/8}\cdots\infty\) is
solution: The exponents form the infinite GP \(\dfrac12+\dfrac14+\dfrac18+\ldots=1\), so the product is \(5^1=5\). Matches option A.

stem: If the second term of a G.P. is 2 and the sum of its infinite terms is 8, then its first term is
solution: \(ar=2\) and \(\dfrac{a}{1-r}=8\). Substituting \(r=\dfrac2a\) gives \(a^2-8a+16=0\Rightarrow (a-4)^2=0\Rightarrow a=4\). Matches option D.

stem: The first term of an infinite G.P. is 1 and every term is equal to the sum of the successive terms, then its fourth term will be
solution: The condition \(ar^{n-1}=\dfrac{ar^{n}}{1-r}\) gives \(1-r=r\Rightarrow r=\dfrac12\). The fourth term is \(\left(\dfrac12\right)^3=\dfrac18\). Matches option B.

stem: If the \((m+n)\)th term of a G.P. is 9 and the \((m-n)\)th term is 4, then the mth term will be
solution: \(T_{m+n}\cdot T_{m-n}=a^2 r^{2m-2}=(a r^{m-1})^2=(T_m)^2=9\times 4=36\), so \(T_m=6\). Matches option A.

subtopic: Harmonic Progressions and the Three Means
stem: If 5 GM's be introduced between 486 and \(\dfrac23\), then the 4th GM is
solution: With 7 terms, \(r^6=\dfrac{2/3}{486}=\dfrac{1}{729}\Rightarrow r=\dfrac13\). 4th GM \(=486\cdot\left(\dfrac13\right)^4=\dfrac{486}{81}=6\). Matches option A.

subtopic: Harmonic Progressions and the Three Means
stem: Find the product of three GM's between 4 and \(\dfrac14\).
solution: Product of n GMs between a and b is \((ab)^{n/2}=\left(4\cdot\dfrac14\right)^{3/2}=1^{3/2}=1\). Matches option A.

subtopic: Harmonic Progressions and the Three Means
stem: If \(a, b, c\) are in HP, then \(\dfrac{a-b}{b-c}\) is equal to
solution: For a, b, c in HP the standard result is \(\dfrac{a-b}{b-c}=\dfrac{a}{c}\). Matches option C.

subtopic: Harmonic Progressions and the Three Means
stem: If the 10th term of an HP is 21 and the 21st term of the same HP is 10, then find the 210th term.
solution: The reciprocals are in AP with \(\dfrac{1}{T_{10}}=\dfrac{1}{21}\), \(\dfrac{1}{T_{21}}=\dfrac{1}{10}\), giving common difference \(\dfrac{1}{210}\) and first reciprocal \(\dfrac{1}{210}\). Then \(\dfrac{1}{T_{210}}=\dfrac{1}{210}+209\cdot\dfrac{1}{210}=1\), so \(T_{210}=1\). Matches option C.

subtopic: Harmonic Progressions and the Three Means
stem: The 6th term of the series \(2, 1\dfrac34, 1\dfrac59, \ldots\) is
solution: The terms are \(2, \dfrac74, \dfrac{14}{9}\); their reciprocals \(\dfrac12, \dfrac47, \dfrac{9}{14}\) are in AP with common difference \(\dfrac{1}{14}\), so \(\dfrac{1}{T_n}=\dfrac{n+6}{14}\) and \(T_n=\dfrac{14}{n+6}\). \(T_6=\dfrac{14}{12}=\dfrac76\). Matches option A.

stem: For any numbers, if A.M. \(=16\) and H.M. \(=\dfrac{63}{4}\), then G.M. will be
solution: \(\text{GM}^2=\text{AM}\times\text{HM}=16\times\dfrac{63}{4}=252\), so \(\text{GM}=\sqrt{252}=6\sqrt7\). Matches option A.

stem: If \(a, b\) and \(c\) are positive real numbers, then \(\dfrac{a}{b}+\dfrac{b}{c}+\dfrac{c}{a}\) is greater than or equal to
solution: By AM-GM, \(\dfrac{a}{b}+\dfrac{b}{c}+\dfrac{c}{a}\ge 3\sqrt[3]{\dfrac{a}{b}\cdot\dfrac{b}{c}\cdot\dfrac{c}{a}}=3\). Matches option A.

stem: If \(A_1, A_2\), \(G_1, G_2\) and \(H_1, H_2\) are two A.M's, G.M's and H.M's between two numbers, then \(\dfrac{A_1+A_2}{H_1+H_2}\cdot\dfrac{H_1 H_2}{G_1 G_2}\) equals
solution: Testing with the numbers 1 and 4: \(A_1+A_2=5\), \(H_1+H_2=\dfrac{10}{3}\), \(H_1 H_2=\dfrac83\), \(G_1 G_2=4\). Then \(\dfrac{5}{10/3}\cdot\dfrac{8/3}{4}=\dfrac32\cdot\dfrac23=1\). Matches option C.

stem: If \(a, b, c \in R^+\) and \(a+b+c=5\), then the maximum value of \(ab^3 c\) is equal to
solution: Split \(b\) into three equal parts: \(a+\dfrac{b}{3}+\dfrac{b}{3}+\dfrac{b}{3}+c=5\). By AM-GM, \(a\cdot\left(\dfrac{b}{3}\right)^3\cdot c\le 1\), so \(ab^3 c\le 27\), attained at \(a=c=1, b=3\). Matches option C.

stem: The sum of the infinite terms of \(1+\dfrac45+\dfrac{7}{5^2}+\dfrac{10}{5^3}+\ldots\) will be
solution: This is an arithmetico-geometric series with \(a=1, d=3, r=\dfrac15\). \(S=\dfrac{a}{1-r}+\dfrac{dr}{(1-r)^2}=\dfrac{1}{4/5}+\dfrac{3/5}{(4/5)^2}=\dfrac54+\dfrac{15}{16}=\dfrac{35}{16}\). Matches option A.

stem: If \(|x|<1\), then the sum of the series \(1+2x+3x^2+4x^3+\ldots\infty\) will be
solution: \(1+2x+3x^2+\ldots=\dfrac{1}{(1-x)^2}\) for \(|x|<1\). Matches option D.

stem: The sum of n terms of the series whose nth term is \(n(n+1)\) is equal to
solution: \(\sum n(n+1)=\sum n^2+\sum n=\dfrac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6}+\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}=\dfrac{n(n+1)(n+2)}{3}\). Matches option A.

stem: \(2+4+7+11+16+\ldots\) up to n terms is equal to
solution: The differences \(2,3,4,5,\ldots\) give \(T_n=1+\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}\). Summing, \(S_n=n+\dfrac{n(n+1)(n+2)}{6}=\dfrac{n}{6}(n^2+3n+8)\). Matches option B.

stem: \(1+3+7+15+31+\ldots\) up to n terms is equal to
solution: Here \(T_n=2^n-1\), so \(S_n=\sum(2^k-1)=(2^{n+1}-2)-n=2^{n+1}-n-2\). Matches option B.
